samples.summary: New 10,000-entry cap on `PUT merges` locks API clients out of documents that legitimately hold more merges, because every other writer of `ws.merges` is uncapped.
samples.evidence: `parseMerges` (worksheet-settings.ts:141) now rejects any body with >10,000 entries, and `PUT merges` is a wholesale replace (worksheet.controller.ts:249). The merge map, however, is also written outside that validator: the editor's collaborative path `YorkieStore.setMerge` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:961/980) appends entries straight into the Yorkie root with no count bound, and `applyMergeRanges` in the XLSX importer (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-importer.ts:258-262) writes one entry per `<mergeCell>` in an uploaded workbook — Excel sheets routinely carry tens of thousands. Once such a document exists, `GET merges` still returns the whole map (worksheet.controller.ts:217) but the natural read-modify-write (GET, drop one entry, PUT) now 400s, and there is no per-anchor delete/patch endpoint to shrink the map instead. The API becomes unable to edit merges on exactly the documents that need it most.

samples.summary: The merge-count guard is reachable-bypassable: the collaborative store and the XLSX import write merges directly to the document, so the unbounded merge-walk cost the cap is meant to prevent is still attainable.
samples.evidence: The new `MaxMergeEntries` doc comment (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:26-43) justifies the cap by the synchronous walks in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, `snapFreezePastMerges` and `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` running inside `doc.update`. But `YorkieStore.setMerge` (yorkie-store.ts:961-982, including the batched branch used by paste) and `applyMergeRanges` (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-importer.ts:258) both write `sheets[tab].merges` without any count check. A document grown past 10,000 merges by those paths is then walked by the *backend* on every `PUT freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:112) and every insert/delete via `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278) — the exact synchronous in-`doc.update` walk the cap claims to bound. If the cap is a real availability control it needs to sit where the map is read/mutated, not only on the one REST body.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is verifiable in the repo. `MaxMergeEntries = 10000` (worksheet-settings.ts:43) causes `parseMerges` to throw BadRequestException for any body with >10,000 entries (worksheet-settings.ts:141-145). `PUT merges` is a wholesale replace: `parseMerges(body)` at worksheet.controller.ts:234 then `ws.merges = merges` at worksheet.controller.ts:249. `GET merges` returns the full uncapped map (worksheet.controller.ts:216-220), so the read-modify-write round-trip is asymmetric and would 400 on any document holding more than 10,000 merges. The two other writers of the same field are genuinely unbounded: `YorkieStore.setMerge` writes `root.sheets[tabId].merges[sref]` with no count check in both the batched path (yorkie-store.ts:969) and the direct path (yorkie-store.ts:980), and `applyMergeRanges` writes one entry per `<mergeCell>` (xlsx-importer.ts:258-259) with no limit anywhere in that file; those imported sheets become real documents via createSpreadsheetDocumentFromImportedXlsxSheets (sheet-import-actions.ts:68). I also confirmed there is no narrowing escape hatch: the controller exposes only GET/PUT for freeze, hidden and merges, and a repo-wide grep for `merges` under packages/backend/src finds no DELETE or PATCH merge route (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:192-193 only shifts existing entries). This is squarely in the blast-radius lane — a new validation at one entry point with sibling writers of the same field left uncapped, producing states the guarded entry point can no longer edit. No guard renders it unreachable and no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `MaxMergeEntries = 10000` (worksheet-settings.ts:43) is enforced only inside `parseMerges` (worksheet-settings.ts:140-145), whose sole caller is `PUT .../merges` (worksheet.controller.ts:234, assigning ws.merges at :249). Its doc comment (lines 25-43) states the cap as an invariant on the worksheet's merge map, justified by the synchronous in-`doc.update` walks. Two other writers reach the same map without any count check: `YorkieStore.setMerge` (yorkie-store.ts:961-982, both the batched branch at 965-970 used by paste and the direct branch at 976-981), driven from sheet.ts:2705, :2944 and :4896; and `applyMergeRanges` (xlsx-importer.ts:258-262), which writes one entry per `<mergeCell>` in an imported file with no cap. Backend consumers then walk the map unconditionally: worksheet.controller.ts:112-116 (`snapFreezePastMerges` inside `doc.update` on every PUT freeze), worksheet-structure.ts:278 (insert/delete shift), worksheet-structure.controller.ts:181/295 (move). No merge-count limit exists anywhere else in packages/sheets or the frontend, so the invariant the cap declares is not upheld on reachable paths. This is the blast-radius lane's "new guard with a way around it"; severity major (reachable bypass of an availability control).
